step1_figure.description: The netlist describes a Class AB amplifier with a push-pull output stage (xmop, xmon) and a floating current source bias. The provided pages (672-682) only cover Class A common-source amplifiers (e.g., Fig 21.17, 21.28), though the text explicitly mentions Class AB amplifiers will be discussed later.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate the load capacitor can be charged or discharged.

equation.explanation: The slew rate is limited by the maximum current the amplifier can source/sink into the load capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes a constant maximum output current I charging a linear capacitor C_L.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a bias current I = 20uA and C_L = 1pF (from Ex 21.5): SR = 20uA / 1pF = 20 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the bias current and load capacitance. Class AB can source much more than quiescent current, so actual SR may be higher.

small_signal_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the amplifier.

equation.explanation: The gain is the transconductance of the input device multiplied by the total output resistance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes low frequency where capacitors act as open circuits.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming I_D = 20uA, W/L = 10. g_m1 = sqrt(2 * 270uA/V^2 * 10 * 20uA) = 328 uA/V. r_o1 = r_o2 = 1 / (0.1 * 20uA) = 500 kOhm. r_o1 || r_o2 = 250 kOhm. A_v = 328uA/V * 250kOhm = 82 V/V = 38.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain is limited by the intrinsic output resistance of the short-channel devices in SKY130.

open_circuit_gain.description: Maximum possible gain attainable with a single MOSFET.

equation.formula: Open circuit gain = -g_m1 * r_o1 = -sqrt(2 * beta_1 * I_D) / (I_D * lambda_1)
equation.explanation: The gain when the MOSFET's load is only its own output resistance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes an ideal current source load with infinite resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using g_m1 = 328 uA/V and r_o1 = 500 kOhm. A_open = 328uA/V * 500kOhm = 164 V/V = 44.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Represents the theoretical maximum gain for a single stage without cascoding.

input_pole.description: The pole associated with the input node of the circuit.

equation.explanation: The input pole is formed by the source resistance and the effective input capacitance, which is increased by the Miller effect.
equation.assumptions: Assumes a finite source resistance R_s.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming R_s = 100kOhm, C_gs1 = 23fF, C_gd1 = 2fF, A_v = 82. C_in = 23fF + 2fF * 83 = 189 fF. f_in = 1 / (2 * pi * 189fF * 100kOhm) = 8.4 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Highly dependent on the external source resistance R_s.

output_pole.description: The pole associated with the output node of the circuit.

equation.explanation: The output pole is formed by the output resistance and the effective output capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes no large external load capacitor or compensation capacitor.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming C_dg2 = 6fF, C_gd1 = 2fF, A_v = 82. C_out = 6fF + 2fF * (1 + 1/82) = 8.02 fF. r_o1 || r_o2 = 250 kOhm. f_out = 1 / (2 * pi * 8.02fF * 250kOhm) = 79.4 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by parasitic capacitances and output resistance.

transfer_function_zero.description: The zero in the transfer function caused by feedforward through C_gd1.

equation.explanation: The zero occurs because the gate-drain capacitance provides a feedforward path that bypasses the transconductance at high frequencies.
equation.assumptions: Assumes C_gd1 is the dominant feedforward path.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using g_m1 = 328 uA/V and C_gd1 = 2fF. f_z = 328uA/V / (2 * pi * 2fF) = 26.1 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Usually at a very high frequency, often beyond the unity-gain bandwidth.

unity_gain_frequency.description: The frequency at which the voltage gain of the amplifier is unity (0 dB).

equation.explanation: The unity-gain frequency is determined by the input transconductance and the compensation (or load) capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes a dominant pole response where f_un >> f_3dB.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a compensation/load capacitor C_c = 1pF and g_m1 = 328 uA/V. f_un = 328uA/V / (2 * pi * 1pF) = 52.2 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scales directly with g_m and inversely with the load/compensation capacitance.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, AC gain, bandwidth, phase margin, and transient slew rate of the Class AB amplifier.
